concerns.text: Task T044 (Plasticity Feature Engineering) is scheduled in Phase 6 but explicitly requires updating `code/04_train_model.py` (T023) to include new features in the nested feature selection loop. T023 is in Phase 4. This creates a circular dependency: T044 depends on T023 being complete, but T044's output is required to correctly implement T023's feature selection logic. T044 must be moved to Phase 3 (after US1 graph metrics are ready) to allow T023 to consume the plasticity features.

Task T018 (Preprocess and Parcellate) is marked `[P]` (parallel-safe). However, it reads `data/processed/eligible_subjects.csv` (output of T017) and writes to `data/processed/connectivity_matrices/`. If T018 runs in parallel with T017 (which is also marked `[P]`), it may attempt to read a file that does not yet exist or is partially written. T018 must be sequential to T017, not parallel.

Task T019 (Compute Graph Metrics) is marked `[P]` but depends on the output of T018 (`data/processed/connectivity_matrices/`). Parallel execution with T018 is impossible. T019 must be sequential to T018.

Task T023 (Train Model) is marked `[P]` but depends on `data/processed/graph_metrics.csv` (T019) and potentially `data/processed/plasticity_features.csv` (T044). It cannot run in parallel with T019 or T044. The `[P]` tag is incorrect.
Task T029 (Permutation Test) imports training logic from `code/04_train_model.py` (T023). It cannot run in parallel with T023. The `[P]` tag is incorrect.

Task T017 is marked `[P]` but is the first data ingestion step. While it has no upstream data dependencies, marking it `[P]` alongside T018/T019 in the same phase implies they can run concurrently, which is false. The `[P]` tag here is misleading in the context of the phase grouping.
